newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian UES plans eurobond no earlier than H2 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russian UES plans eurobond no earlier than H2 1997.

text.p: Russia's national power company Unified Energy System (UES) is considering issuing a Eurobond, but this will not happen before the second half of next year, UES officials said on Thursday.
The issue appears to be replacing an earlier plan by the government to issue a Eurobond convertible into 7.5 percent of UES shares.
That plan was dropped after the government decided to auction 8.5 percent of UES, including the 7.5 percent intended for the convertible Eurobond, for cash next month.

Alexander Lopatin, UES (RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii) asset management director, said the company was considering an issue of Eurobonds to draw funds for investment projects to develop power stations and lines, but that there were no concrete plans yet.
"We are now considering Eurobonds, to be issued by UES itself, and now we know what to do to achieve it," Lopatin said.
"Under the best scenario this may happen in the second half of 1997."
He reiterated that the issue would not be convertible into 7.5 percent of UES shares.
Russia's privatisation ministry, the State Property Committee (GKI), has dropped an earlier plan it announced in September to issue a Eurobond convertible into 7.50 percent of UES in December.
Instead it is planning an auction with bids accepted from November 22 to December 23, of 3.66 billion shares or 8.5 percent of UES.
The issue would have been Russia's first convertible Eurobond.
GKI sources said the issue had been initially delayed because UES, Russia's biggest company by sales and employees, and one of its most liquid shares, was "insufficiently open".
A source at UES said the advisers to the issue had said it was not technically possible to undertake such a complicated financial transaction by the end of the year.
UES has not yet published financials restated to international accounting standards, but has announced plans to issue American Depositary Receipts.
Altogether the government owns 60 percent of UES, but has said it will keep 51 percent until 1998.
Two other large companies, gas monopoly RAO Gazprom and Russia's biggest oil group, NK LUKoil, are talking of doing corporate Eurobonds.
Russia's debut sovereign Eurobond was heavily oversubscribed last week, despite the volume being increased to $1 billion and maturity extended to five years.
